result.title: Understanding Gene Expression-to-Image Learning: Spatial Structure and Information Fidelity
result.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables cell-level analysis of biological heterogeneity, but learning effective representations from high-dimensional, unordered gene expression profiles remains challenging. Gene Expression-to-Image (GE2I) offers an effective learning strategy by arranging gene values on pixel grids for convolutional neural networks, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We study GE2I on full-transcriptome data while keeping the network and training procedure fixed. Our results reveal a trade-off between spatial smoothness and gene-level fidelity. Structured mappings produce smooth, low-frequency patterns that support faster early optimization, whereas assigning multiple genes to the same pixel obscures expression differences and can reduce predictive performance. This trade-off explains why random mappings can compete with structured layouts when many genes are represented. One-to-one gene-to-pixel assignment improves prediction across the tested visual backbones even when image smoothness decreases. We further find that the benefits of pretraining and augmentation depend on the backbone and mapping. These findings provide practical guidance for pixel allocation and the transfer of vision priors to gene expression data.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在固定网络与训练流程下研究基因表达到图像（GE2I）的学习机制，发现空间平滑性与基因级保真度之间的权衡：多个基因共用一个像素会模糊表达差异，而一对一基因—像素映射在多个视觉骨干上提升预测，且预训练与增强的收益依赖骨干与映射方式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「空间平滑性 vs 信息保真度」权衡以及多基因挤占同一像素导致差异被模糊的现象，可能与 LVR 中视觉细节被压入有限 latent 槽位时的信息坍缩问题形成类比，可供核查。
